newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai police raid brokerages after bank rumours.
newsitem.headline: Thai police raid brokerages after bank rumours.

text.p: Police on Thursday raided offices of at least two foreign brokerages to investigate if they were behind rumours that some medium and small Thai banks might be suspended by the authorities, industry sources said.

"Police walked in and questioned our staff and executives... we told them that our company recently overweighted Thailand, so there is no reason why we should spread such rumours," said an official of ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett, one of the two houses raided.
Staff at another brokerage, also said to have been raided, declined to comment whether police had searched their office and the firm's management could not be reached for comment.
Officers at a special police unit set up by Deputy Interior Minister Chalerm Yubamrung to screen press reports said they were not aware of the raids.
Government spokesmen last week said rumours about troubled Thai banks were spread by fax messages to other countries by some equities research houses that held malicious views on Thailand.

The country is going through its worst economic slump in more than a decade with severe problems in its financial and property sectors. On July 2, the authorities floated the baht, which led to a de fact devaluation of between 15 and 20 percent.
Bangkok Metropolitan Bank Plc, Siam City Bank Plc, Bank of Asia Plc, First Bangkok City Bank Plc, and Thai Danu Bank Plc have denied they were potential targets of suspension by the government.
The Bank of Thailand also denied the rumours.
But the talk caused a slide in prices on the Thai stock market as investors steered clear of some banking stocks.

Former finance minister Amnuay Viravan, his adviser and former deputy central bank governor Ekamol Khiriwat, and Viroj Nualka, chairman of Phatra Thanakit Plc, on Thursday denied Thai press speculation they might have been behind the rumours against the banks.
Amnuay said in a statement the rumours against the banks were fabricated and he would take legal action against people or newspapers further suggesting that he and his advisers were behind them.
